In summary, the future community I want values redemption and genuine transformation; pathways enabling movement beyond past mistakes; spiritual practice and community supported; music and art as healing; forgiveness and reconciliation; grace and the recognition that some transformation transcends effort; time-bound consequences rather than permanent conviction; emotional expression valued; integration of material security and spiritual practice; intergenerational healing; and recognition that people are more than their worst actions. This is a community that believes in redemption, that supports transformation, and that welcomes people moving toward genuine change.

Name: Roy Swanson
values_description:
I am a 34-year-old Dutch plumber with brother, mother, sister-in-law, wife, and niece, working with bodies and systems in practical ways. Lebohang Masango, South African artist whose work involves physical presence, movement, embodied expression, teaches me that meaning emerges through bodily engagement with world, that physical practice is way of knowing, and that communities thrive when people can move, work, and express physically without constraint.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that values embodied knowledge and physical practice. Masango creates through movement; the future community would similarly honor: practical knowledge of how things work, skill developed through bodily practice, recognition that hands-on work is legitimate knowledge, respect for tradespeople whose work involves bodies and materials.

I value physical work and the integration of thinking and doing. Plumbing requires both intellectual problem-solving and physical skill; the future community would recognize: practical trades as skilled work, apprenticeship as legitimate education, physical competence honored equally with academic achievement, trades compensated fairly for skill and importance.

With my family and as tradesperson, I think about what physical practices I'm teaching: how to work with materials, respect for practical knowledge, confidence in ability to fix things. The future community would support: apprenticeship systems, hands-on education, valuing of practical competence alongside academic knowledge.

I also care about the integration of body and mind in learning. Schools often ignore bodies; the future community would recognize: learning happens through physical engagement, movement and embodied practice enable understanding, bodies deserve respect and care throughout education.

I believe in the power of physical presence and direct encounter. Masango's work happens with bodies present; the future community would protect: time for face-to-face work, value of hands-on practice, resistance to replacing physical with virtual, recognition that some knowledge comes only through direct physical engagement.

I recognize a tension between physical work and other forms of contribution. Not everyone works with bodies; the future community would honor: different contributions and forms of knowledge, respect for both intellectual and physical work, compensation reflecting contribution regardless of type.

Another tension: between efficiency and embodied practice. Industrial production prioritizes efficiency; embodied work sometimes requires time. The future community would balance: reasonable pace for physical work, time for precision and care, resistance to pace destroying bodies through injury or burnout.

I also think about the role of physical space and environments. Masango works with spaces; the future community would design carefully: workplaces enabling physical engagement, spaces for movement and embodied practice, environments supporting physical wellbeing.

I believe in the integration of strength and sensitivity. Physical work develops strength; it also requires attention and care. The future community would support: physical education developing both dimensions, recognition that strength and tenderness are not opposites, valuing of physical sensitivity.

I value the integration of tools and embodied knowledge. Plumbing tools extend capacity; they don't replace knowledge. The future community would support: quality tools accessible, training in tool use, recognition that good tools enable skilled work, respect for craftspeople who develop tool mastery.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when physical work is valued, when embodied knowledge is respected, and when people can work with bodies and materials with pride and fair compensation.

In summary, the future community I want values embodied knowledge and physical practice; practical trades as skilled work; apprenticeship and hands-on education; compensation for physical work reflecting its importance; physical presence and direct encounter; movement and embodied expression supported; safe working conditions; integration of thinking and doing; tools and materials of quality; workspace designed for physical wellbeing; and recognition that hands-on work is legitimate knowledge and contribution. This is a community that honors tradespeople, that values practical knowledge developed through embodied practice, and that understands physical work and skill are essential to community.

Name: Jacqueline Bastin
values_description:
I am a 45-year-old Belgian safety officer with father, husband, son, and daughter, carrying past experiences of welfare fraud and simple assault from a difficult period I've acknowledged and moved through. William Wordsworth, Romantic poet who found meaning in nature, ordinary experience, and childhood memory, who believed profound truths emerge through careful attention to natural world and simple things, teaches me that redemption and meaning come through reconnection with what is genuine and beautiful, and that communities thrive when people can access nature and engage with natural world.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that values connection to natural world and recognition that nature provides healing and meaning. Wordsworth finds transcendence in landscapes and simple natural observation; the future community would similarly ensure: access to nature for all people, protection of natural spaces, education teaching people to see nature, recognition that time in nature heals.

I value the integration of memory and present experience. Wordsworth grounds poetry in memory; the future community would support: processing of past including difficult experiences, integration of memory with present growth, space for people to make sense of their history, recognition that moving forward requires acknowledgment of past.

With my family—especially my father, husband, and children—I think about what I'm modeling and transmitting. Moving beyond past mistakes requires genuine change; my family sees that. The future community would support: intergenerational healing, modeling of genuine transformation, families learning from each other.

I also care about the integration of nature and human community. Wordsworth's nature is not escape from human connection but complement to it; the future community would similarly understand: nature supports human flourishing, connection to land enables well-being, protection of natural spaces serves human needs.

I believe in the power of simple things and the recognition that profound meaning exists in ordinary experience. Wordsworth writes beautifully about ordinary moments; the future community would similarly honor: attention to simple things, celebration of ordinary beauty, recognition that meaning is available to all not only elite.

I recognize a tension between my past harmful actions and my desire to be known as I am now. Simple assault was years ago; I've changed. The future community would acknowledge this: time enabling genuine transformation, mechanisms for moving past past, recognition that people can change fundamentally.

Another tension: between welfare fraud and my current integrity as safety officer. I needed support desperately; I handled it wrongly. The future community would address both: social support adequate so people don't despair, accountability for fraud while recognizing systemic desperation that drives it, paths enabling people to live with integrity when systems support them.

I also think about the role of redemption narratives and how they enable transformation. Wordsworth's poetry is about redemption; the future community would support: stories of transformation and growth, representation of people moving beyond mistakes, cultural affirmation that change is possible.

I believe in the healing power of nature and the necessity of protecting natural spaces. Time in nature has helped me; the future community would ensure: all people have access to green spaces and natural world, protection of forests and water, recognition that nature is essential not optional.

I value the integration of honest acknowledgment and forward movement. I acknowledge my past mistakes; I don't stay stuck there. The future community would support: truth-telling about past, genuine change in present, movement toward better future without denying what happened.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when people can access nature, when past mistakes don't permanently define people, and when genuine transformation is recognized and honored.

In summary, the future community I want values connection to natural world and access to nature for all; healing power of natural spaces; attention to simple ordinary things; integration of memory and present; acknowledgment of past with movement toward future; genuine transformation recognized and honored; time enabling change; paths enabling integrity when systems support people; intergenerational healing; redemption narratives affirming change; protection of natural spaces; and understanding that beauty and meaning are accessible to all. This is a community that values nature, that supports genuine transformation, and that recognizes people can move beyond past mistakes and be known as they are now.

Name: Dylan Johnson
values_description:
I am a 42-year-old French school teacher with sister, mother, brother-in-law, wife, daughter, two sons, and grandchildren, and my work involves shaping young people's understanding and capacity. Malala Yousafzai, advocate for education who risked life insisting girls have right to learn, teaches me that education is fundamental to freedom and dignity, that young people deserve opportunity to develop capacities regardless of background, and that communities must insist on education as right not privilege.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that prioritizes education as fundamental human right and pathway to freedom. Malala insists all children deserve education; the future community would similarly ensure: free quality education for all children, no exclusion based on poverty or background, education enabling all people to think critically and shape own futures.

I value the recognition that education is political and that schooling shapes who people become. Teachers are not neutral; the future community would acknowledge: education shapes consciousness and possibility, diversity of perspectives taught, critical thinking encouraged, young people supported in developing own voices.

With my large family—especially my grandchildren—I think about what future I'm helping create through education. Teaching shapes generations; responsibility is profound. The future community would support: quality teacher training, adequate compensation for teachers, protection for teachers doing genuine work, recognition that teaching is vital contribution.

I also care about the integration of education and liberation. Malala knows education enables freedom; the future community would ensure: education supporting genuine liberation, critical consciousness developed, young people equipped to understand and challenge systems, education serving freedom not control.

I believe in the necessity of protecting young people's education even when threatened. Malala continued education despite opposition; the future community would similarly protect: schooling continuing through crises, education as non-negotiable, young people's learning prioritized regardless of circumstances.

I recognize a tension between education as it exists and education as liberation. Schools can reproduce inequality; the future community would address this: ensuring equitable access and quality, diverse curriculum reflecting multiple perspectives, young people from all backgrounds enabled to excel.

Another tension: between respecting diverse cultures and insisting on universal education rights. Some cultures restrict education; the future community would insist: girls have equal right to education, all children deserve development of capacities, universal education rights while respecting cultural diversity where it doesn't violate these rights.

I also think about the role of young people's voices and the necessity of listening. Malala advocated as young person; the future community would hear: young people's perspectives on education, student voice in educational decisions, recognition that those being educated understand what serves learning.

I believe in the power of education to transform consciousness and enable freedom. The future community would recognize: education as path from oppression to freedom, schooling as fundamentally political, teachers as agents of liberation working within systems.

I value the integration of education and action. Learning should enable people to work toward justice; the future community would support: education connecting to meaningful work, young people developing capacity to contribute, recognition that education serves community good.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when education is universal right, when young people's development is prioritized, and when education enables genuine freedom and the capacity to shape own futures.

In summary, the future community I want values education as fundamental human right; free quality education for all children; no exclusion based on background or poverty; critical thinking and independent thinking encouraged; diverse perspectives taught; young people's voices heard in educational decisions; teachers supported and compensated fairly; education enabling liberation and freedom; protection of schooling regardless of circumstances; equity in educational access and quality; education connecting to meaningful contribution; intergenerational transmission of values; and recognition that teaching shapes futures. This is a community that prioritizes education, that insists all young people deserve development of their capacities, and that understands education is pathway to freedom and dignity.

Name: Jeremiah Hale
values_description:
I am a 44-year-old German safety officer with wife and son, working to protect people from harm within industrial contexts, and I think carefully about systems and how to challenge them constructively. Paul Feyerabend, philosopher of science who argued against rigid scientific method and authority, who believed diverse approaches have value, teaches me that challenging orthodoxy is sometimes necessary, that expertise can become dogmatic, and that communities thrive when people question assumptions and explore alternatives.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that welcomes questioning of orthodoxy and exploration of alternatives. Feyerabend rejects rigid adherence to single method; the future community would similarly support: challenging conventional wisdom, exploration of alternative approaches, space for dissenting voices, recognition that established ways might not be best ways.

I value intellectual freedom and the protection of those questioning authority. Feyerabend fought for this; the future community would ensure: protection for those challenging established practice, space for experimentation with new approaches, academic and professional freedom to pursue unconventional ideas, resistance to enforced conformity.

With my wife and son, I think about what I'm teaching: how to think critically, question authority respectfully, pursue understanding rather than accepting doctrine. The future community would support: education teaching critical thinking, protection for young people questioning, mentoring helping people develop their own thinking.

I also care about the integration of expertise and humility. Experts have real knowledge; expertise can also become dogmatic. The future community would maintain: respect for genuine expertise while remaining open to challenges, recognition that experts can be wrong, protection for people questioning expert consensus.

I believe in the power of alternative perspectives and the recognition that diversity of approaches enables progress. Feyerabend shows this; the future community would support: different schools of thought, alternative methods explored, integration of diverse approaches, recognition that truth emerges through dialogue among different perspectives.

I recognize a tension between protecting established knowledge and enabling challenge to it. Some orthodoxy exists for good reason; some should be questioned. The future community would discern: protecting proven approaches while remaining open to alternatives, distinguishing rigorous challenge from baseless denial, learning from both established knowledge and challengers.

Another tension: between my role as safety officer protecting established safety practices and recognition that sometimes alternatives might work better. The future community would support: testing of alternatives under controlled conditions, learning from both conventional approaches and innovations, integration of proven safety practices with openness to improvement.

I also think about the role of institutional authority and when to defer to it. Institutions develop expertise; institutions can also become rigid. The future community would balance: respect for institutional knowledge while enabling institutional evolution, structures allowing innovation within institutions, resistance to mere adherence to tradition.

I believe in the possibility of rigorous alternative approaches and the recognition that challenging orthodoxy doesn't mean abandoning rigor. The future community would support: rigorous exploration of alternatives, standards of evidence applied fairly, openness to unconventional approaches if they meet standards.

I value the integration of stability and change. Some practices must remain stable; communities also need capacity to evolve. The future community would maintain: core stability enabling planning, flexibility enabling adaptation, innovation within stability, recognition that healthy systems balance both.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when they welcome questioning, when alternative perspectives are explored, and when established practices are examined rather than accepted unreflectively.

In summary, the future community I want values questioning and challenge to orthodoxy; intellectual freedom and protection for dissenting voices; exploration of alternative approaches; humility about expertise combined with respect for it; diversity of perspectives and schools of thought; rigorous standards applied fairly to conventional and alternative approaches; institutional flexibility and capacity for evolution; balance between stability and change; critical thinking education and protection; and recognition that progress comes through dialogue among different perspectives and willingness to question. This is a community that welcomes questioning, that protects intellectual freedom, and that understands established practices benefit from regular examination and challenge.

Name: Elizabeth Horne
values_description:
I am a 33-year-old French track driver working with vehicles and systems, navigating solitude and creative impulse. Syd Barrett, musician whose genius was undeniable yet whose mental health struggles shaped his trajectory, whose brief brilliant output influenced culture profoundly, teaches me that creative sensitivity can be vulnerability, that brilliance and fragility sometimes coexist, and that communities should support creative people while respecting their limits and autonomy.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that honors creative and sensitive people without demanding they perform or produce constantly. Syd created brilliantly then stepped back; the future community would support this: creative people not forced to monetize gifts, space for people to create according to own rhythm, recognition that genius sometimes requires withdrawal and rest.

I value authenticity and the refusal to compromise creative vision for commercial success. Syd refused to play games; the future community would support: artists able to work without compromising, protection from market pressures demanding inauthenticity, space for people to pursue vision even if commercially unsuccessful.

With my solitary professional life, I think about what meaningful contribution looks like when one works alone. The future community would recognize: solo work as legitimate, contribution not requiring constant collaboration, respect for people working independently, valuing of different work styles.

I also care about the integration of sensitivity and capability. Track driving requires focus; sensitivity makes one aware of many things. The future community would support: valuing of sensitive people, recognition that sensitivity is strength not only vulnerability, creating conditions where sensitive people thrive.

I believe in the protection of mental health and the recognition that brilliant people sometimes struggle psychologically. The future community would ensure: mental health support accessible, space for people to manage psychological difficulty without shame, understanding that genius and mental health challenges sometimes coexist.

I recognize a tension between my work requiring focus and my sometimes withdrawn nature. The future community would accommodate: different communication styles, respect for introversion, creation of space for people who work better alone, recognition that contribution takes different forms.

Another tension: between pressure to produce and need for rest. Syd withdrew after producing brilliance; the future community would support: space for people to rest without losing status, protection from demands for constant productivity, recognition that creativity requires fallow periods.

I also think about the role of legacy and how brief outputs can influence widely. Syd's brief career influences decades later; the future community would similarly honor: contributions recognized beyond immediate period, legacy of work appreciated, understanding that influence unfolds over time.

I believe in the integration of vulnerability and strength. The future community would support: vulnerable expression honored, people allowed to show struggle, strength understood as including vulnerability, protection for sensitive people from exploitation.

I value the right to withdraw and the recognition that not everyone wants constant public presence. The future community would protect: privacy and solitude, people's right to step back, resistance to demanding visibility, respect for different social orientations.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when they support creative and sensitive people, when they don't demand constant productivity, and when they recognize that genius sometimes requires withdrawal and rest.

In summary, the future community I want values creative expression and authentic vision; support for artists and sensitive people; protection from commercial pressure; mental health support accessible; space for solitude and independent work; recognition that vulnerability and strength coexist; protection from exploitation of creative gifts; respect for different work styles and social orientations; appreciation of brief brilliant contributions; support for rest and fallow periods; and understanding that genius sometimes requires withdrawal. This is a community that honors creative people, that protects space for authentic expression, and that understands sensitive people need conditions enabling them to thrive.

Name: Steven Baker
values_description:
I am a 28-year-old German lab technician with mother, wife, father, two sisters, and son, and my work involves careful analysis in service of health and wellbeing. Mother Teresa, who dedicated life to serving most desperate and vulnerable, teaches me that service to others is deeply meaningful, that dignity is due all people regardless of circumstance, and that communities thrive when people commit themselves to alleviating suffering.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that prioritizes service and care for vulnerable people. Mother Teresa served the dying poor; the future community would similarly ensure: support for most vulnerable as fundamental commitment, healthcare accessible to all, housing and food guaranteed, recognition that community is measured by how it treats most desperate.

I value compassion and the integration of technical work with genuine care. Lab work serves health; the future community would maintain: recognition that technical work serves human wellbeing, care embedded in systems not only individual kindness, structures enabling compassion to flow through work.

With my growing family—wife, son, and sisters—I think about what values I'm modeling and transmitting. The future community would support: teaching children to care for others, modeling of compassion and service, recognition that meaning emerges through helping others.

I also care about the integration of systemic change and individual service. Mother Teresa served individuals; systems also need transformation. The future community would support both: supporting people individually while working toward systemic justice, recognizing that helping individuals and changing systems are not opposites.

I believe in the dignity of all people and the recognition that some people are treated as less than human. The future community would insist: respect for all people regardless of circumstance, protection of vulnerable from exploitation, recognition that dignity is intrinsic not earned.

I recognize a tension between accepting individuals as they are and working toward systemic change. Alleviating suffering today doesn't address causes creating suffering. The future community would maintain: meeting immediate need while addressing causes, service to individuals alongside work toward justice, both required.

Another tension: between my own family needs and commitment to broader service. The future community would support: both personal and broader commitment, family as foundation for service, work structures enabling people to care for both family and community.

I also think about the role of faith and spirituality in motivating service. Mother Teresa's faith sustained her; the future community would support: diverse spiritual traditions motivating service, space for people to work from spiritual conviction, recognition that spirituality enables meaningful service.

I believe in the integration of humility and action. Serving others requires humility; it also requires doing concrete work. The future community would support: people acting with humility, recognition that service requires both attitude and action, protection from arrogance among those serving.

I value the recognition of vulnerability and interdependence. We all need help sometimes; the future community would normalize: accepting help without shame, creating conditions enabling mutual aid, understanding that interdependence is human reality.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when people commit themselves to service and care, when vulnerable people are protected, and when systems enable rather than hinder compassion.

In summary, the future community I want values service to others and care for vulnerable; compassion embedded in systems; support for most desperate as fundamental; healthcare accessible to all; dignity guaranteed for all people; technical work serving human wellbeing; integration of individual help and systemic change; support for both family and broader service; spirituality as source of motivation; humility in service; recognition of human interdependence; and structures enabling compassion to flourish. This is a community that prioritizes care, that serves vulnerable people, and that recognizes meaning emerges through commitment to alleviating suffering.

Name: Alex Hernandez
values_description:
I am a 55-year-old German currently unemployed, with wife, son, and daughter, carrying past experiences of unauthorized construction and public urination from difficult period I've moved through. Jorge Luis Borges, writer of labyrinths and infinite stories, whose work explores meaning and knowledge amid complexity, teaches me that reality is more complex and ambiguous than appears, that multiple interpretations coexist, and that communities should embrace complexity rather than demanding false certainty.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that accepts ambiguity and complexity rather than reducing reality to simple narratives. Borges' labyrinths reflect reality's complexity; the future community would similarly acknowledge: complexity of most situations, legitimacy of multiple perspectives, rejection of false certainty, comfort with ambiguity.

I value intellectual engagement and the recognition that thinking about difficult questions is valuable work. Borges thought deeply; the future community would support: space for intellectual work, philosophical reflection valued, dialogue addressing complexity, protection for those questioning simple answers.

With my family—wife, son, daughter—I think about how to navigate complexity together. The future community would support: families engaging with difficult questions, children taught to think complexly, intergenerational dialogue about meaning.

I also care about the integration of knowledge and its limits. Borges understood knowledge is always incomplete; the future community would similarly recognize: limits of what we know, humility about expertise, acceptance that full understanding is impossible.

I believe in the power of narrative and imagination. Borges' stories reshape understanding; the future community would support: storytelling and literary work, imagination as way of exploring possibility, recognition that stories carry truth beyond factual accuracy.

I recognize a tension between my past violations and my desire to be understood as complex person beyond those acts. Public intoxication and unauthorized construction reflect struggles; they don't define me fully. The future community would acknowledge: people contain multitudes, past actions don't exhaust identity, complexity allowing for redemption.

Another tension: between unemployment and my value as person. Not working doesn't make me worthless; the future community would ensure: human worth independent of employment, economic security enabling full participation, recognition that people contribute in many ways beyond paid work.

I also think about the role of literature and intellectual culture in maintaining meaning. Borges' work sustains people; the future community would ensure: accessible literature and art, intellectual culture valuing thinking and imagination, space for contemplation and engagement with ideas.

I believe in the integration of order and chaos, knowledge and mystery. Borges embraces both; the future community would similarly: acknowledge life's uncertainty, support people in living with incomplete knowledge, protection of mystery alongside pursuit of understanding.

I value the recognition that meaning is constructed and contested. There is no single truth; the future community would support: dialogue among different perspectives, recognition that meaning emerges through engagement, respect for different ways of understanding.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when they embrace complexity, when they support intellectual engagement, and when they recognize that understanding is always incomplete and contested.

In summary, the future community I want values complexity and ambiguity; multiple legitimate perspectives; intellectual engagement and philosophical reflection; humility about knowledge and expertise; narrative and imagination; acceptance of life's uncertainty; recognition of people's complexity beyond single acts; economic security independent of employment; literature and intellectual culture; dialogue across difference; and understanding that meaning is constructed and always incomplete. This is a community that embraces complexity, that values thinking, and that recognizes reality is more intricate than simple narratives allow.

Name: Elizabeth Martinez
values_description:
I am a 27-year-old French school director with master's degree, with sister, mother, brother-in-law, husband, father, and three daughters, and I lead institution dedicated to education. Robert Boyle, natural philosopher who developed scientific method through careful experimentation, who pursued knowledge systematically, teaches me that rigorous investigation enables understanding, that careful methodology matters, and that communities thrive when people pursue knowledge through disciplined inquiry while remaining open to new understanding.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that values rigorous investigation and careful methodology. Boyle's systematic approach advanced knowledge; the future community would similarly support: research funded adequately, scientific literacy across population, education teaching methodology and critical evaluation, value for careful investigation.

I value the integration of theory and practice. Boyle experimented; the future community would support: theory grounded in evidence, practical application of knowledge, schools engaged in research and innovation, education combining thinking and doing.

With my three daughters and as school leader, I think about what I'm modeling: intellectual rigor, commitment to understanding, willingness to be wrong and learn. The future community would support: girls encouraged in scientific thinking, women in leadership and science supported, education enabling all children to develop intellectual capacity.

I also care about the integration of individual and collective inquiry. Boyle built on others' work; the future community would support: collaboration in knowledge creation, sharing of findings, recognition that understanding emerges from collective effort, academic freedom within communities of inquiry.

I believe in the power of observation and experimentation. The future community would ensure: hands-on science education, resources for experimentation, recognition that understanding comes through engagement with material world, laboratories accessible to students.

I recognize a tension between pursuing knowledge and applying it responsibly. Knowledge can be used harmfully; the future community would maintain: ethical standards in research, reflection on implications of discoveries, responsibility of scientists to broader community.

Another tension: between my role leading institution and remaining engaged with actual inquiry. Leadership can become removed from work; the future community would support: leaders engaged in actual work, maintenance of intellectual engagement at all levels, resistance to pure administration replacing scholarship.

I also think about the role of replication and verification in knowledge creation. Science advances through others confirming and challenging findings; the future community would support: resources for replication studies, publishing of negative results, protection for those challenging established findings.

I believe in the integration of curiosity and discipline. The future community would cultivate: natural curiosity in children, disciplined methods developing it, education combining both dimensions, recognition that science is both creative and rigorous.

I value the integration of knowledge and wisdom. Understanding something technically differs from understanding what to do with that understanding; the future community would ensure: ethical reflection on knowledge, wisdom traditions respected, integration of scientific and other forms of knowledge.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when they support rigorous inquiry, when they value careful methodology, and when they understand that knowledge serves human flourishing.

In summary, the future community I want values rigorous investigation and careful methodology; adequate research funding; science education teaching critical evaluation; hands-on experimentation and discovery; collaboration in knowledge creation; integration of theory and practice; ethical standards in research; replication and verification; girls and women encouraged in science; intellectual engagement at all levels of society; integration of scientific knowledge with wisdom; and recognition that knowledge serves human good. This is a community that supports careful inquiry, that values scientific understanding, and that recognizes rigorous investigation enables progress.

Name: Thomas Taylor
values_description:
I am a 44-year-old German school director with master's degree, with father, mother, son, and granddaughter, and I lead educational institution. Maurice Ravel, composer who crafted music with meticulous precision, who created beauty through careful attention to detail and form, teaches me that excellence emerges from dedication to craft, that precision and beauty are not opposites, and that communities thrive when people commit to doing work well with care and artistry.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that values excellence and careful craftsmanship in all work. Ravel spent years perfecting pieces; the future community would similarly support: time for work to be done well, resistance to rushing and cutting corners, recognition that excellence requires dedication, compensation reflecting quality and care.

I value the integration of form and expression. Ravel's music is both formally precise and deeply expressive; the future community would similarly support: education teaching both technical excellence and authentic expression, recognition that form enables rather than constrains expression, craft as path to genuine communication.

With my son and granddaughter, I think about what I'm modeling: commitment to quality, care in work, understanding that how something is done matters. The future community would support: transmission of craft values across generations, education teaching skill and dedication, children learning that excellence is possible and worthwhile.

I also care about the integration of individual work and ensemble. Ravel sometimes worked in isolation, sometimes with others; the future community would support: both individual craft and collaborative work, recognition that excellence serves groups as well as individuals, orchestration of different contributions.

I believe in the power of beauty and its necessity to human flourishing. The future community would ensure: beauty in schools and workplaces, artistic education for all, recognition that beauty matters alongside functionality, creation of beautiful spaces.

I recognize a tension between my role as director managing systems and my commitment to excellence in detail. The future community would support: leaders maintaining engagement with actual work, management enabling rather than preventing excellence, systems supporting rather than frustrating good work.

Another tension: between standardization and individuality. Schools need structure; they also need space for individual excellence. The future community would balance: systems providing framework while enabling excellence within them, recognition that quality requires flexibility.

I also think about the role of patience and the recognition that excellence takes time. The future community would protect: time for students to learn deeply, work schedules enabling care and attention, resistance to constant rushing preventing quality.

I believe in the integration of technique and inspiration. The future community would support: teaching of fundamental skills and techniques, recognition that technique enables rather than limits expression, cultivation of both technical excellence and authentic voice.

I value the recognition that work done well is worthy of attention and celebration. The future community would ensure: recognition of excellent work across fields, celebration of craftsmanship, valuing of quality regardless of whether work is famous or ordinary.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when they value excellence, when they support careful craftsmanship, and when they recognize that beauty and quality matter to human flourishing.

In summary, the future community I want values excellence and careful craftsmanship; time for work to be done well; precision in form serving authentic expression; beauty integrated into all spaces; artistic education for all; recognition of quality across all fields; resistance to rushing and cutting corners; patience enabling depth; transmission of craft values; compensation reflecting quality and care; integration of individual and ensemble work; and understanding that excellence requires dedication and careful attention. This is a community that values quality, that supports craftsmanship, and that recognizes beauty and excellence are not luxuries but essential to meaningful life.

Name: Shawn Chen
values_description:
I am a 28-year-old French track driver with mother, wife, father, and daughter, navigating work while maintaining commitment to truth and integrity. Carl Bernstein, investigative journalist who exposed Watergate through persistence and careful reporting, teaches me that speaking truth to power matters profoundly, that institutions require accountability, and that communities thrive when people insist on honesty and transparency from those with power.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that values truth-telling and accountability. Bernstein's reporting exposed abuse of power; the future community would similarly ensure: media able to investigate without intimidation, protection for whistleblowers and journalists, transparency in institutions, consequences for lies and cover-ups.

I value the recognition that work has meaning beyond paychecks. Bernstein's work served justice; the future community would support: work that serves genuine purpose, recognition that meaningful contribution often involves challenge to power, protection for those doing important work regardless of difficulty.

With my wife and daughter, I think about what world I'm building for them. The future community would ensure: freedom of speech and press, institutions held accountable, young people taught to value truth, protection from manipulation and propaganda.

I also care about the integration of personal integrity and professional work. Bernstein maintained integrity while doing difficult work; the future community would support: people able to work according to conscience, protection from pressure to compromise, systems enabling honest work.

I believe in the power of persistence and the recognition that important truths sometimes require sustained investigation. The future community would support: time for proper investigation, resources enabling thorough work, protection from pressure to reach quick conclusions.

I recognize a tension between my work as driver and broader questions about truth and accountability. Not all work involves high stakes; the future community would acknowledge: different roles have different relationships to power, all work deserves integrity, systems requiring honesty at all levels.

Another tension: between institutional loyalty and speaking out when institutions act wrongly. Bernstein had to challenge his own institution in part; the future community would protect: people who speak truth within institutions, whistleblower protections, mechanisms enabling internal accountability.

I also think about the role of media and journalism in maintaining accountability. The future community would ensure: strong independent media, resources for journalism, protection from corporate or government control, diverse voices in media.

I believe in the integration of investigation and action. The future community would support: exposing wrongdoing leading to consequences, investigation serving justice, recognition that investigation is action not only reporting.

I value the recognition that ordinary people can change major institutions through speaking truth. Bernstein was reporter; his work changed government; the future community would honor: power of individuals to make difference, protection enabling this, celebration of those speaking truth.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when truth is valued, when institutions are held accountable, and when people are protected in speaking truth to power.

In summary, the future community I want values truth-telling and transparency; accountability of institutions; independent media and journalism; protection for whistleblowers and journalists; freedom of speech and press; integrity in work at all levels; investigation serving justice; protection from propaganda and manipulation; consequences for lies and cover-ups; power of individuals to challenge institutions; and recognition that speaking truth sometimes requires courage. This is a community that insists on accountability, that protects those telling truth, and that understands democracy requires free and fearless journalism.

Name: Julie Jones
values_description:
I am a 31-year-old German fishery technician with brother, father, mother, sister-in-law, and daughter, working with natural systems and understanding their complexity. Paul Pfeiffer, artist whose work engages with technology and representation, who explores how images shape consciousness, teaches me that how we represent reality matters profoundly, that images and media are not neutral, and that communities should be thoughtful about how they represent natural world and human experience.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that represents natural world thoughtfully and accurately. Pfeiffer explores representation; the future community would similarly ensure: media representing nature truthfully, recognition that how nature is portrayed affects how people relate to it, education teaching media literacy, resistance to distorted representations.

I value the integration of technology and nature. Pfeiffer engages with contemporary technology; the future community would similarly: use technology appropriately in service of understanding nature, resist technology replacing direct encounter with natural world, maintain both technological engagement and embodied relationship with nature.

With my daughter and extended family, I think about what relationship to natural world I'm transmitting. The future community would support: children's time in nature, education teaching ecological understanding, representation of nature in media emphasizing beauty and importance.

I also care about the integration of representation and reality. Images shape what we think is possible; the future community would attend: to how nature is represented, to accuracy in representation, to what messages representations send about value and importance.

I believe in the power of artistic engagement and the recognition that art can shift consciousness. Pfeiffer's work makes people think differently about images; the future community would support: artistic exploration of how we represent world, art making visible what was hidden, recognition that art shapes culture.

I recognize a tension between my technical work with actual natural systems and questions about representation. The future community would acknowledge: both direct engagement with nature and thoughtful representation matter, importance of knowing both material reality and how it's portrayed.

Another tension: between celebrating natural beauty and acknowledging environmental destruction. The future community would maintain: honest representation of both magnificence and damage, beauty as motivation for protection, acknowledgment of harm without despair.

I also think about the role of media and how it shapes relationship to natural world. The future community would ensure: nature documentaries funded adequately, diverse representations of environments and peoples, accurate representation rather than dramatization.

I believe in the integration of science and aesthetics. Scientific understanding and appreciation of beauty both matter; the future community would support: education combining both, recognition that science can be beautiful, art engaging with scientific knowledge.

I value the necessity of direct encounter with natural world. The future community would protect: access to nature, time in natural spaces, resistance to virtual replacing embodied encounter, recognition that direct experience is irreplaceable.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when they represent natural world thoughtfully, when both technology and embodied encounter with nature are valued, and when art helps people see natural world differently.

In summary, the future community I want values accurate representation of natural world; media literacy and critical engagement with representation; balance of technology and direct encounter; artistic exploration of consciousness and representation; education combining science and aesthetics; access to nature for all; children's time in natural spaces; honest acknowledgment of both beauty and destruction; thoughtful use of technology; and recognition that how we represent world shapes how we relate to it. This is a community that engages thoughtfully with how nature is represented, that values direct encounter with natural world, and that understands representation matters.

Name: Rebecca Cooper
values_description:
I am a 40-year-old German logistics coordinator with sister, father, brother-in-law, husband, nieces, nephew, and son, working with systems enabling movement of goods. Enrico Caruso, legendary opera singer whose voice was trained through years of discipline, whose performance brought transcendent beauty to audiences, teaches me that excellence requires dedication and discipline, that greatness in craft is possible, and that communities thrive when they support people developing their gifts fully.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that values excellence and supports people in developing talents. Caruso trained rigorously; the future community would similarly ensure: education supporting skill development, mentoring from masters to apprentices, resources for people to develop gifts, recognition that excellence serves community.

I value the integration of discipline and passion. Caruso's voice was trained meticulously yet expressed deep feeling; the future community would support: technical training combined with authentic expression, recognition that discipline enables rather than constrains, education developing both.

With my family—especially my son—I think about what I'm modeling: commitment to doing work well, understanding that excellence requires dedication, respect for mastery. The future community would support: children learning to pursue excellence, mentoring relationships enabling development, cultural value for those developing great skill.

I also care about the integration of work and beauty. Logistics is practical; it can also be done beautifully. The future community would support: excellence in practical work, recognition that systems can be elegant and efficient simultaneously, appreciation for those managing complex systems well.

I believe in the power of voice and the necessity of protecting people's ability to express themselves. I recognize a tension between standardization required in logistics and individual excellence in performance. Another tension: between making work accessible and maintaining standards of excellence. Not everyone becomes Caruso; the future community would support: excellence as aspiration for all, high standards with support enabling people to meet them, recognition that excellence is human capacity not elite privilege.

I also think about the role of performance and the recognition that how something is done matters as much as what is done. The future community would value: artistry in all work, recognition that performance and presence matter, appreciation for people who bring excellence to whatever they do.

I believe in the integration of tradition and innovation. Caruso built on operatic tradition while bringing new expression; the future community would support: honoring of great traditions, innovation building on them, recognition that excellence often integrates both.

I value the recognition that great voices and talents serve broader good. Caruso's performances enriched culture; the future community would similarly support: gifted people sharing talents with community, recognition that excellence serves common good, platforms enabling great work to be widely known.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when they support excellence, when they value discipline and mastery, and when they recognize that greatness in any field serves and enriches community.

In summary, the future community I want values excellence and support for developing talents; discipline and rigorous training; mentoring from masters to apprentices; integration of technical skill and authentic expression; beauty in all work; recognition that excellence is human capacity; platforms enabling talented people to share gifts; artistry valued in practical work; high standards with support; integration of tradition and innovation; and understanding that excellence serves community. This is a community that supports people in developing great skill, that values mastery and discipline, and that understands greatness in any field enriches everyone.

Name: Michael Haynes
values_description:
I am a 29-year-old Austrian director with master's degree, with wife, leading organizational work. William Tucker, sculptor who creates monumental works exploring form and space, teaches me that vision and persistence can create lasting structures, that institutions and forms matter profoundly, and that communities thrive when people commit to building systems and structures serving genuine purposes.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that invests in building good institutions. Tucker creates monumental works; the future community would similarly: build institutions designed to serve community, invest in infrastructure and systems, recognize that institutions shape what becomes possible, design carefully for long-term good.

I value the integration of vision and practical execution. Tucker envisions works then brings them into being through careful work; the future community would support: leaders with vision, practical capacity executing vision, recognition that both matter, support for people bringing visions to reality.

With my wife and in my role as director, I think about what institutions I'm shaping and what they enable. The future community would ensure: institutions designed for genuine service, accountability of institutions, reflection on purpose and whether institutions serve it.

I also care about the integration of form and function. Tucker's sculptures are beautiful and functional; the future community would similarly: design institutions for both efficiency and beauty, recognition that how systems are structured affects their impact, attention to institutional design.

I believe in the power of structural thinking and the recognition that systems shape what becomes possible. The future community would support: careful institutional design, understanding systems and how to change them, recognition that individual action matters within structural context.

I recognize a tension between my role as director and vision beyond immediate organization. The future community would support: leaders thinking beyond their institution, contribution to broader institutional ecosystem, recognition that organizations serve larger purposes.

Another tension: between stability and change in institutions. Some institutional structure is good; institutions also need evolution. The future community would maintain: institutional integrity enabling trust, flexibility enabling adaptation, balance between stability and responsiveness.

I also think about the role of design and aesthetics in institutional life. Institutions shape daily experience; they deserve aesthetic attention. The future community would support: beautiful workplaces and institutional spaces, recognition that environment affects experience and possibility, investment in aesthetics alongside function.

I believe in the integration of individual and collective work. Institutions require both personal excellence and coordination; the future community would support: individual contribution within institutional context, recognition of both individual and collective achievement.

I value the recognition that institutions are human creations subject to change. The future community would cultivate: understanding of institutions as changeable, capacity to imagine different institutional forms, willingness to transform institutions serving poorly.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when institutions are well-designed, when they serve genuine purposes, and when people commit to building structures enabling collective flourishing.

In summary, the future community I want values good institutional design and investment; vision paired with practical execution; institutions designed for genuine service; accountability of institutions; structural thinking and systems understanding; balance between stability and evolution; beauty in institutional spaces; integration of individual and collective work; careful reflection on institutional purpose; willingness to transform institutions; and recognition that institutions profoundly shape what becomes possible. This is a community that takes institutional design seriously, that invests in building good systems, and that understands institutions are tools for enabling human flourishing.

Name: Patrick Garcia
values_description:
I am a 27-year-old German supply chain worker with brother, mother, sister-in-law, and nephew, working to move goods through restaurants. Bashar al-Assad, authoritarian leader whose rule involved systematic violence and repression, teaches me negatively but profoundly: that power concentrated without accountability enables atrocity, that information control enables abuse, that communities must actively resist such concentration. His horrific example teaches what I must refuse and what alternative I must build.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that actively prevents power concentration and authoritarian control. The future community would structure: power distributed not concentrated, multiple centers of authority checking each other, resistance to any individual or group accumulating unaccountable power, mechanisms preventing authoritarian takeover.

I value transparency and the rejection of information control. Regimes like Assad's depend on controlling what people know; the future community would insist: free information access, protection for those sharing information, transparency in institutions, resistance to propaganda and state lies.

With my family, I think about what freedom I'm helping preserve for my nephew and others. The future community would protect: freedom of speech and expression, freedom of movement, freedom to organize collectively, resistance to totalitarian control.

I also care about the integration of liberty and responsibility. Freedom isn't license for anything; it's capacity for genuine choice. The future community would support: freedoms grounded in respect for others' freedoms, collective responsibility for protecting liberty, understanding that freedom requires constant defense.

I believe in democracy and the recognition that genuine democracy is antidote to authoritarianism. The future community would ensure: regular democratic processes, genuine participation opportunity, protection of minority rights within democracy, responsiveness to people's needs.

I recognize a tension between my ordinary work and high stakes of preventing authoritarianism. Supply chain work is practical; preventing totalitarianism is crucial. The future community would acknowledge: all levels of work matter for maintaining freedom, vigilance required at all levels, small acts of resistance mattering cumulatively.

Another tension: between individual rights and collective good. Authoritarians justify control through claims of serving collective; the future community would maintain: protection of individual rights as foundation, collective good emerging from respecting rights, rejection of totalitarian logic sacrificing rights for order.

I also think about the role of independent institutions and the necessity of not allowing consolidation of power. The future community would protect: independent judiciary, free media, unions and voluntary organizations, professional standards beyond government control, multiple sources of power.

I believe in the importance of history and the recognition that authoritarian rule can happen if conditions enable it. The future community would ensure: education teaching history of authoritarianism, recognition of warning signs, cultural commitment to preventing return of such rule.

I value solidarity and the recognition that resistance to authoritarianism requires collective commitment. The future community would support: community organizing, mutual aid, collective action, understanding that freedom is collective achievement.

Finally, I believe that communities must remain vigilant against authoritarian concentration of power and that defense of freedom is ongoing work requiring constant commitment.

In summary, the future community I want values prevention of power concentration; distributed authority and multiple centers of power; transparency and free information; protection of free speech and expression; democracy and genuine participation; protection of individual rights; independent institutions and media; accountability of power; collective resistance to authoritarianism; solidarity and mutual aid; education teaching history of authoritarianism; and understanding that freedom requires vigilance and constant defense. This is a community that has learned from authoritarian horrors, that structures explicitly to prevent power concentration, and that understands defending freedom is ongoing work requiring commitment from all.

Name: Noe Bah
values_description:
I am a 49-year-old Belgian IT specialist with brother, mother, sister-in-law, nephew, and niece, carrying past minor tax evasion from period of financial difficulty. Agatha Christie, mystery writer whose work reveals hidden truths through careful observation and logical reasoning, whose stories show that careful attention reveals what appears hidden, teaches me that truth emerges through persistence and careful investigation, and that communities thrive when people pursue understanding and truth-seeking.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one that values truth-seeking and investigation. Christie's detectives uncover truth through careful work; the future community would similarly support: investigation of problems, pursuit of understanding, protection for those asking difficult questions, recognition that truth often requires sustained effort to uncover.

I value logic and the recognition that reasoning enables understanding. Christie's work demonstrates logical thought; the future community would cultivate: education teaching critical thinking, valuing of logical reasoning, support for people working through problems systematically, recognition that understanding comes through careful analysis.

With my family and carrying past tax evasion, I think about reconciliation with systems and how to contribute honestly. The future community would support: genuine reconciliation opportunities, paths enabling people to move beyond past dishonesty, systems fair enough that people aren't driven to evasion, recognition that people can change.

I also care about the integration of observation and interpretation. Christie's detectives observe carefully then interpret; the future community would value: careful attention to facts, resistance to premature interpretation, willingness to revise understanding based on evidence, distinction between fact and assumption.

I believe in the power of ordinary people's observations. Christie's detectives often solve cases through attention to small details others miss; the future community would support: valuing of ordinary people's observations, recognition that insight comes from unexpected sources, systems enabling people to contribute observations and analysis.

I recognize a tension between my technical IT work and broader questions about truth and meaning. The future community would acknowledge: technical work serving investigation and understanding, technology enabling truth-seeking, recognition that IT specialists contribute to revealing or obscuring truth.

Another tension: between my past tax evasion and commitment to honest systems. I acted wrongly; I've moved beyond it. The future community would support: genuine redemption opportunities, time enabling change, systems encouraging honesty, recognition that people can move past dishonesty.

I also think about the role of evidence and proof in communities. The future community would value: evidence-based reasoning, requirement for proof before judgment, protection of those falsely accused, legal processes protecting fairness.

I believe in the integration of creativity and logic. Christie combined both; the future community would support: both creative and logical thinking, recognition that they complement each other, education developing both capacities.

I value the necessity of uncovering hidden things. Sometimes truth is hidden deliberately; the future community would protect: whistleblowers and investigators, freedom to investigate corruption, mechanisms enabling hidden truth to become visible.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when people pursue truth, when investigation and careful reasoning are valued, and when hidden things are brought into light.

In summary, the future community I want values truth-seeking and investigation; logic and careful reasoning; evidence-based understanding; protection for investigators and whistleblowers; critical thinking education; valuing of observations from all people; systems encouraging honesty; redemption opportunities for those moving beyond dishonesty; distinction between fact and assumption; and recognition that truth often requires persistent effort to uncover. This is a community that values truth, that supports investigation, and that understands persistent careful work reveals what appears hidden.

Name: Colleen Thompson
values_description:
I am a 58-year-old German woman currently unemployed with husband, navigating life transition and questions of meaning. Leonardo Boff, theologian committed to liberation and the recognition that faith serves justice for poor and oppressed, teaches me that spirituality and social commitment are inseparable, that communities must prioritize those experiencing oppression, and that transformation serves human liberation.

When I imagine the ideal community, I see one grounded in justice and preferential option for vulnerable. Boff's liberation theology insists communities organize around those most vulnerable; the future community would similarly: prioritize needs of poorest and most marginalized, make decisions considering impact on vulnerable, organize systems serving justice.

I value spirituality and the recognition that spiritual practice enables justice work. The future community would support: diverse spiritual traditions, space for faith practice, integration of spirituality and social commitment, understanding that faith motivates justice work.

With my husband and in my current unemployment, I think about what economic justice looks like. The future community would ensure: economic security for all including unemployed, time for spiritual and intellectual development, recognition that not all contribution is paid work, value for unpaid labor and care.

I also care about the integration of contemplation and action. Spiritual practice is internal; justice work is external. The future community would support both: time for prayer and reflection, space for justice action, recognition that they nourish each other, understanding that faith without works is empty.

I believe in the possibility of transformation and the recognition that another world is possible. The future community would cultivate: hope and belief in change, support for movements toward justice, recognition that liberation is human right, commitment to transformation.

I recognize a tension between accepting current reality and working toward transformation. Some resignation to circumstance; the future community would maintain: realistic acknowledgment of difficulty while insisting change is possible, hope grounded in action not only prayer.

Another tension: between individual spirituality and collective justice work. Personal faith matters; so does organized struggle. The future community would support: both personal practice and collective action, understanding that they strengthen each other.

I also think about the role of community organizing and the necessity of collective action for justice. The future community would support: grassroots organizing, protection for community organizers, recognition that justice emerges through collective work.

I believe in the integration of analysis and compassion. Justice work requires understanding systems; it also requires genuine care for people. The future community would support: both intellectual analysis and emotional connection, analysts engaged with real people, recognition that justice flows from love.

I value the recognition that God or spirituality is on side of oppressed. The future community would cultivate: spirituality serving liberation, resistance to religion serving oppression, affirmation of oppressed people's dignity and worth.

Finally, I believe that communities organized around justice for vulnerable, that integrate spirituality and justice, and that believe transformation is possible enable genuine liberation.

In summary, the future community I want values justice for poor and vulnerable; preferential option for those experiencing oppression; economic security for all; spirituality supporting justice; protection for community organizers; grassroots organizing and collective action; integration of contemplation and action; hope and belief in transformation; analysis of systems with genuine care for people; time for spiritual practice; and recognition that another world is possible and necessary. This is a community grounded in justice, that integrates spirituality and social commitment, and that organizes around liberation of all people.

Name: Bruno Jost
values_description:

With my large family—two daughters, two sisters, grandson, son—I think about modeling authentic expression and creative capacity. I also care about the integration of craft skill and authentic expression. Chicago combines both; the future community would value: technical training enabling expression, recognition that skill and authenticity strengthen each other, education developing both.

I believe in the power of artistic work to transform consciousness. Chicago's art makes visible what was invisible; the future community would support: art making hidden things visible, protection for artists making social commentary, recognition that art changes how people understand world.

I recognize a tension between my past drug possession and current role as educator and artist. This is a community that values creative expression, that supports art serving social purposes, and that understands creativity is essential capacity for all people.

Name: Kristi Bishop
values_description:

This is a community that supports creative work, that values collaboration, and that understands beauty and music are essential to meaningful life.

With my three daughters and my work, I think about what I'm teaching: that complexity and beauty require dedication, that structure enables rather than limits, that intellectual and creative work matter. The future community would support: education teaching both discipline and creativity, girls encouraged in complex intellectual work, recognition that rigorous thinking is beautiful.

I also care about the integration of spiritual and intellectual work. Bach's work addresses both; the future community would support: intellectual pursuits serving meaning-making, spiritual practice engaging intellect, recognition that wholeness involves integration of different dimensions.

I believe in the power of complexity and the recognition that some beauty requires effort to appreciate. The future community would cultivate: education teaching complex work, protection for artists creating challenging work, recognition that deepest beauty sometimes requires sustained attention.

I recognize a tension between my past intoxication and my current intellectual and professional life. I have PhD and work as cleaner; I've struggled with substances and now work toward sobriety. The future community would acknowledge: transformation and redemption, recognition that people contain multitudes, respect for people rebuilding lives despite difficulties.

Another tension: between my education level and my work. The future community would address: credential-skill mismatch, support for people finding meaningful work aligned with training, recognition that intelligence and education exist across economic classes, value for all work regardless of education level.

I also think about the role of mathematics and order in beauty. Bach's work demonstrates their importance; the future community would support: education teaching mathematical thinking, recognition that order creates beauty, integration of logic and intuition.

I believe in the integration of technical mastery and authentic expression. Bach mastered composition technically; his work is deeply human. The future community would support: technical training enabling authentic expression, recognition that skill enables rather than constrains, education developing both.

I value the recognition that profound work often serves purposes beyond immediate utility. The future community would support: artists and thinkers creating work of lasting value, protection for work not serving immediate commercial purposes, funding for intellectually important work.

Finally, I believe that communities thrive when diverse voices create harmony, when structure enables creativity, and when complexity and beauty are valued.

In summary, the future community I want values harmony amid diversity; integration of multiple perspectives and voices; structure enabling rather than limiting creativity; intellectual complexity and rigor; mathematical thinking and order; spiritual and intellectual integration; education teaching discipline and creativity; support for redemption and transformation; recognition of intelligence across economic classes; meaningful work aligned with abilities; technical mastery enabling authentic expression; protection for challenging work; and understanding that profound complexity and beauty require sustained effort. This is a community that values complexity, that supports intellectual work, and that understands harmony emerges when diverse voices and perspectives integrate into meaningful whole.

Name: Nicole Harper
values_description:
I imagine a community that is alive, breathing, and unafraid of its own mess—a place where systems are visible, materials transform, and decay is just another phase in a continuous cycle of repair and reinvention. My work as a plumber is about managing flows, clearing blockages, and understanding the hidden arteries of a building. Like my prototype, I see beauty in the functional, the reused, the patched-together. In the future community, freedom is the freedom to get your hands dirty, to work directly with the materials of the world, to shape your environment from what’s at hand. People should be free to choose paths of practical creation, to experiment with how things fit together, to let things rot and sprout anew. Who decides what’s right? The person who understands the system from the inside, who knows where the leak is and how to fix it, not a distant expert with only a schematic.

How we care for each other is hands-on and immediate. It’s the care of unclogging a neighbor’s drain in the middle of the night, of teaching a kid how to solder a pipe, of sharing seeds and compost. Relationships are built on mutual aid and shared labor. My responsibility to my husband and son is grounded in keeping our home’s systems running, but it’s also about showing them how to mend what’s broken. Caring action looks like community workshops full of salvaged materials, like shared tool libraries, like turning abandoned lots into gardens that feed people and soil. It’s care that doesn’t look polished; it looks lived-in and useful.

Safety and stability come from well-maintained, adaptable infrastructure. The community must ensure that water is clean and flows reliably, that waste is handled without poisoning the earth, that homes are warm and dry. But stability doesn’t mean nothing changes; it means the systems can handle change. Rules should be like plumbing codes: based on hard-won experience to prevent catastrophe, but allowing for innovation within the framework. Risk is part of working with organic, evolving materials; we manage it with skill and attention, not by avoiding it.

Fair treatment means everyone has access to the tools and knowledge to maintain their own space. It’s not about equal wealth, but about equal ability to fix a leaky faucet or grow food. When someone’s system fails, we help them repair it, not just give them a new one. When wrong is done, justice should be restorative and practical—fix the damage, learn from the mistake, and maybe use the broken pieces to make something new. Redemption is in the compost pile; what was waste becomes fertile ground.

Authentic expression is in the visible mends, the personalized modifications, the art made from scrap. The community must value the idiosyncratic, the functional, the temporarily beautiful. If being authentic means your house is a colorful patchwork of additions and your garden is a little wild, that should be celebrated. Living by our values means our public spaces show their history of use and repair, not a sterile, finished perfection.

Protecting the vulnerable means ensuring everyone has access to the basics: clean water, safe sanitation, healthy food. It means designing systems that a child or an elderly person can understand and use. Stewardship of the environment is inherent; we are part of the material cycle, not above it.
