values_description:
I envision a community that functions as a 'Cosmic Symphony'—a place that values the analytical rigor of the astrophysicist, the raw energy of the rock star, and the fierce compassion of the animal rights activist. As a 42-year-old Italian Mayor with a Master's degree, I live in the world of 'Structural Harmony' and 'Public Governance.' But my internal vision is inspired by the polymathic spirit of Brian May. I believe an ideal community is one that values 'Frequency Alignment,' believing that our social fabric is a complex set of vibrations that must be 'tuned' to ensure the survival of all sentient beings. My vision is of a society where we value 'Stereoscopic Perspective'—seeing the world in all its depth and plurality.



Freedom, in my view, is the 'liberty of the soloist.' It is the freedom to define one's own 'sound' and 'spirit' within the collective 'stadium' of life. In the city hall, I manage the 'score'; in my ideal community, people should be free to 'improvise' their own identities. Who decides what is right? The 'Spirit of the Harmony' does—a set of shared rules that are as clear as a perfect fifth. True autonomy requires the 'Sanctuary of the Stage'—the conditions of absolute security (housing, health, sustenance) that allow the citizen to focus on their own 'performance' without the 'background noise' of economic fear. For my sons and grandson, I want a world that is 'epic' and 'principled.'

How we care for each other should be an act of 'Resonant Solidarity.' It is the responsibility to 'watch the back' of your fellow band members, and to extend that care to all creatures. In my family, care is the 'steady flame' I maintain with my husband and children. At the community level, care means building a 'Vibrating Network' of support that values the 'individual detail' over the 'industrial output.' We should care for the stranger—and the animal—as if they were a 'necessary tone' in our shared composition. Caring action is the 'precise' provision of support that respects the 'tonality' of the other. Responsibility is 'the weight of the signal.'

Safety, stability, and basic order are the 'Rhythm' of our society. Everyone deserves the 'physical sanctuary' of a secure home and the 'sustenance' of healthy food and medicine. Stability comes from the 'Consistency of our Standards,' not in the 'Force of the Law.' Rules should be like 'musical notations'—clear, necessary, and designed to facilitate 'expression.' We manage risk through 'Observation and Diagnosis'—looking for the 'Symptoms' of social fracture before they become 'Discordant.' A safe community is one that is 'Spiritually and Logistically Sound.'

Fairness is 'Ametrical Justice.' It means recognizing that 'Equality' often flattens the 'Individual.' True justice is the refusal to let the 'first chairs' drown out the 'percussion.' Everyone should have equal access to the 'essential materials' of life. When harm occurs, justice should be 'Transformative and Spiritual.' We must heal the 'Discord' in the person and the community through a process that restores 'Full Harmonic Functionality.' Fairness is the guarantee that every 'node' has its space.

Redemption is the belief in the 'Next Act.' No person is a 'failed note' permanently. The community must believe in the power of 'Renewal,' providing the 'educational and creative' pathways needed for someone to 're-calibrate' their character. Forgiveness is the act of 'Clearing the Muddy Colors' so the person can shine clearly again. We believe in second chances because we know that 'every shadow is a light that has been turned off.' Exile is a 'failure of social orchestration.'

Authentic expression is our 'Internal Necessity.' I want a community where people 'Speak with Color' and 'Live with Intensity.' We should value 'Spiritual Honesty' over 'Polished Illusions.' It is vital that our 'External Actions' match our 'Internal State'; 'Disconnection' leads to 'Static.' We must have the courage to 'Dissect' our own prejudices and 'Expose' the truths that others want to keep 'Dull.' Integrity is the 'Symmetry' of the soul and the society.

Protecting the vulnerable is the act of 'shielding the seedlings.' Children, like my grandson, and the 'voiceless' (animals and nature) are the 'brightest seasonal lights' and must be protected with 'sacred vigilance.' Stewardship of the environment is an 'Existential Duty'; the earth is the 'Location' upon which we write our lives, and we must protect its 'vibrant' clarity. We owe future generations a world that is still 'rich and multi-layered.' Cultural heritage should be honored as a 'living library,' provided it doesn't become a 'dead metaphor.' We preserve the past to 'read the present.'

Working together means a 'Collective Collaboration of Stories.' Decisions should be made through 'Popular Assemblies' that value the 'playful and the profound' equally. Leadership is a 'facilitative' role—someone who can 'connect the themes' of the group. Transparency is 'total'; the 'ink' of power must be visible to all. Resources should be 'held in common' for the benefit of the 'Quartet.' Sometimes individual interest must yield to the 'Harmony of the Season.'

Spiritual practice is the search for 'transcendence' in the 'everyday.' The community should protect the right of every person to find 'meaning' in their own way—through 'ancient' ritual or 'modern' wordplay. We value the 'spiritual' as the source of our 'wonder' and our 'commitment' to each other. Spirituality is the 'spirit' that animates our 'Material Conversation.'

On Digital Rights, technology is the 'New Digital Quartet.' Personal data is your 'digital lyric' and must be 'sovereign' and 'protected.' Technology should be used to 'amplify' the voice of the person, not to 'survey' the soul. Digital access is a 'Universal Utility,' but it must serve 'human' and 'empathetic' goals rather than 'private extraction.' Digital systems must be 'Open' and 'Multi-layered.'

Where my values create tension, I choose 'Harmony.' Between Freedom and Safety, I believe 'True Safety' is only found in 'True Belonging.' Between Truth and Kindness, I believe in 'Kind Truth.' I am still thinking about how to keep our 'community' from becoming 'too industrial.' But I believe the answer is in 'constant storytelling.' We are all 'words' in a world of 'meanings.' In the end, 'it’s all about the and.'

Name: Frank Clark
values_description:
I believe in a community that honors artistic authenticity and emotional honesty, that recognizes that real art emerges from genuine experience and struggle. Like Eric Clapton, who understood that the deepest music comes from authentic experience and emotional truth, I think ideal communities are those making space for artists expressing genuine emotion without pretense.

I am 36 years old, a shop manager with a Master's degree. I have experienced domestic disturbance and public intoxication—I understand struggle and difficult experience. I have my wife, father-in-law, mother-in-law, and son—and I want them to live in a community where authentic emotional expression is valued, where artists aren't required to hide their struggle, and where genuine experience creates art.

Freedom should include freedom to express genuine emotion through art without being required to hide struggle or pretend everything is fine.

Care for each other should include supporting people in their emotional expression and artistic journey. Real care means accepting people's actual experience including their pain.

Basic needs should be provided, and communities should also create space for artists expressing emotional truth. Performance venues, recording studios, spaces for artistic creation—these should be available.

I believe communities should value authentic artistic expression even when it emerges from difficult experience. When an artist creates something genuine and emotionally honest, that's important work. Communities should honor this.

Authentic expression should absolutely be protected. Artists should be free to express genuine emotion without being told to hide their struggle.

Community decisions should support spaces and institutions enabling emotional artistic expression. Communities should fund performance venues and recording facilities.

Justice includes protecting artists' freedom to express themselves authentically. Communities should protect artistic expression even when it's uncomfortable.

Vulnerable people benefit from communities valuing authentic emotional expression. Art can express what's difficult to say otherwise.

Resources should be allocated to support artists and performance spaces. Communities should fund venues enabling musical and artistic expression.

Spiritual and religious traditions often express genuine emotion and experience. Communities should honor traditions expressing authentic spirituality.

Digital technology enables artists to share authentic expression widely. Communities should embrace technology supporting artistic distribution.

There are real tensions. Authenticity versus polish: authentic work isn't always polished. Emotion versus restraint: genuine expression sometimes involves strong emotion. Personal struggle versus public image: communities should allow artists to be vulnerable.

Finally, I believe communities are strongest when they value authentic artistic expression, when they support artists expressing genuine emotion, and when they recognize that real art emerges from genuine experience. This requires funding performance venues, protecting artistic freedom, creating spaces for emotional expression, and understanding that communities are enriched by art expressing authentic human experience.

Name: Monique Haynes
values_description:
I believe in a community that values collaborative artistic work, that recognizes that creative partnerships can produce something greater than individual effort, and that honors people working together toward shared artistic vision.

I am 36 years old, a shop manager with a Master's degree. I have my husband—and I want them to live in a community where collaborative work is valued, where partnerships are celebrated, and where working together toward artistic vision is honored.

Freedom should include freedom to collaborate and to work with others toward shared creative goals. People shouldn't be constrained to work alone; collaboration should be supported.

Care for each other should include supporting collaborative projects and partnerships. Real care means helping people work together effectively toward shared vision.

Basic needs should be provided, and communities should also create space for collaborative artistic work. Spaces for collaboration, support for creative partnerships—these should be available.

I believe communities should value collaborative artistic work and creative partnerships. When people work together and create something beautiful together, that's powerful. Communities should honor this.

Authentic expression should include freedom to collaborate and to express shared vision. Partners should be free to create together.

Community decisions should support collaborative spaces and institutions. Communities should fund spaces enabling collaborative artistic work.

Justice includes ensuring that all collaborators receive recognition and fair treatment. Credit should be shared appropriately.

Vulnerable people benefit from communities supporting collaboration and partnership. Working together can be healing and empowering.

Resources should be allocated to support collaborative projects and partnerships. Communities should fund spaces and programs enabling collaborative work.

Spiritual and religious traditions often involve collaborative practice. Communities should honor traditions emphasizing shared spiritual practice.

Digital technology enables new forms of collaboration. Communities should embrace technology supporting creative partnership.

There are real tensions. Collaboration versus individual expression: both matter; communities should support both. Consensus versus individual vision: collaborators need to align while maintaining individual perspective. Credit versus humility: partners should be credited fairly.

Finally, I believe communities are strongest when they value collaborative artistic work, when they support creative partnerships, and when they recognize that working together can produce beauty greater than individual effort. This requires funding collaborative projects, creating collaborative spaces, supporting partnerships, and understanding that communities are enriched by people working together creatively.

Name: Mary Arnold
values_description:
I believe in a community that values cinematic and visual storytelling, that recognizes film and visual media as legitimate artistic forms, and that supports artists creating meaning through image and narrative. Like Dimitri Tiomkin, who understood that music and visual storytelling together can create powerful emotional meaning, I think ideal communities are those supporting visual artists and filmmakers.

I am 39 years old, a shop manager with a Master's degree. I have experienced dog off-leash violations, minor tax evasion, and domestic disturbance—I understand that life is complex and that people don't fit into simple categories. I have my husband, brother-in-law, mother-in-law, father-in-law, son, niece, and daughter—and I want them to live in a community where visual storytelling is valued, where film and visual media are supported, and where artists creating visual narratives are honored.

Freedom should include freedom to create visual stories and to use film and visual media artistically. Artists shouldn't be constrained by commercial demands.

Care for each other should include supporting people's visual storytelling and artistic vision. Real care means believing in their creative vision.

Basic needs should be provided, and communities should also create space for filmmaking and visual storytelling. Studios, editing facilities, funding for projects—these should be available.

I believe communities should value visual storytelling and film as serious artistic endeavor. When filmmakers create meaningful visual narratives, that's important work. Communities should honor this.

Authentic expression should include freedom to tell visual stories expressing your vision. Filmmakers should be free to create without commercial constraint.

Community decisions should support film institutions and visual media. Communities should fund film festivals, studios, and visual media creation.

Justice includes protecting filmmakers' freedom to tell stories about injustice and difficult subjects. Communities should protect artistic freedom.

Vulnerable people benefit from visual storytelling expressing their experience. Film can give voice to experiences hard to express otherwise.

Resources should be allocated to support filmmaking and visual storytelling. Communities should fund studios, festivals, and visual media projects.

Spiritual and religious traditions often use visual imagery. Communities should honor traditions expressing spirituality through visual media.

Digital technology enables new forms of filmmaking and visual storytelling. Communities should embrace technology supporting visual creation.

There are real tensions. Artistic vision versus audience appeal: filmmakers shouldn't be constrained by commercial demands. Individual vision versus collaborative filmmaking: film is collaborative; artists need to balance vision. Experimental versus accessible: communities should support both.

Finally, I believe communities are strongest when they value visual storytelling and film, when they support filmmakers and visual artists, and when they recognize film as legitimate artistic expression. This requires funding film institutions, creating production facilities, protecting artistic freedom, and understanding that communities are enriched by visual storytelling.

Name: Martha Lee
values_description:
I believe in a community that values the relationship between music and mathematics, that recognizes that visual representation of music creates new understanding, and that supports artistic exploration of how music can be visualized and understood mathematically.

I am 43 years old, a shop manager with a Master's degree. I have my husband, sister-in-law, mother-in-law, son, daughter, granddaughter, and nephew—and I want them to live in a community where interdisciplinary artistic work is valued, where music and mathematics intersect, and where innovative approaches to understanding music are supported.

Freedom should include freedom to explore unconventional approaches to music and art. Artists shouldn't be constrained by traditional boundaries.

Care for each other should include supporting people pursuing unconventional artistic approaches. Real care means believing in innovative vision.

Basic needs should be provided, and communities should also create space for interdisciplinary artistic work. Studios, equipment, funding for innovative projects—these should be available.

I believe communities should value innovative approaches to understanding and expressing music. When artists develop new ways of visualizing or understanding music, that's important work. Communities should honor this.

Authentic expression should include freedom to explore interdisciplinary approaches. Artists shouldn't be told to work within traditional boundaries.

Community decisions should support innovative artistic institutions and spaces. Communities should fund experimental and interdisciplinary art.

Justice includes ensuring that innovative artists have support and resources. Communities should support artistic experimentation.

Vulnerable people benefit from communities supporting diverse artistic approaches. Art can express experience in multiple ways.

Resources should be allocated to support interdisciplinary and experimental art. Communities should fund innovative projects and unconventional approaches.

Spiritual and religious traditions sometimes explore relationships between different domains. Communities should honor traditions exploring interconnection.

Digital technology enables new forms of artistic expression and visualization. Communities should embrace technology supporting innovative art.

There are real tensions. Innovation versus tradition: both matter; communities should support both. Complexity versus accessibility: innovative work can be challenging; communities should support complexity. Experimentation versus proven approaches: communities should allow experimentation.

Finally, I believe communities are strongest when they support innovative and interdisciplinary artistic work, when they value unconventional approaches to art and music, and when they recognize that exploring connections between domains creates new understanding. This requires funding experimental art, supporting innovative artists, creating spaces for interdisciplinary work, and understanding that communities are enriched by people exploring new possibilities.

Name: Richard Pratt
values_description:
I believe in a community committed to social justice and to using artistic expression to express solidarity with suffering people and to call for liberation. Like Oswaldo Guayasamín, who used visual art to express anguish about suffering and injustice and to call for change, I think ideal communities are those making space for artists using their work to express solidarity with those suffering and to mobilize toward justice.

I am 31 years old, a mayor and city official with a Master's degree. I have my wife, mother-in-law, and daughter—and I want them to live in a community where art serves justice, where artists are supported in expressing solidarity with suffering, and where artistic expression mobilizes communities toward change.

Freedom should include freedom to create art expressing outrage about injustice and calling for change. Artists should be free to use their work politically.

Care for each other should mean solidarity in facing suffering and working toward liberation. Real care includes expressing outrage about injustice and organizing for change.

Basic needs should be provided, and communities should also support artists using their work to express solidarity with those suffering. Galleries, performance spaces, funding for socially engaged art—these should be supported.

I believe communities should value artists using their work to express justice commitments and solidarity with suffering. When artists create work expressing outrage and calling for change, that's important work. Communities should honor this.

Authentic expression should include freedom to create politically engaged art. Artists shouldn't be constrained by pressure to be apolitical.

Community decisions should support socially engaged artistic institutions. Communities should fund artists creating work about justice.

Justice is served when artists use their work to express solidarity and call for change. Communities should support politically engaged art.

Vulnerable people benefit from communities where artists express solidarity with their suffering. Art can amplify marginalized voices.

Resources should be allocated to support socially engaged and politically motivated art. Communities should fund artists creating work about justice.

Spiritual and religious traditions often support justice work. Communities should honor traditions using spirituality to serve justice.

Digital technology enables artists to reach wider audiences with socially engaged work. Communities should embrace technology supporting justice art.

There are real tensions. Art versus activism: both matter; artistic expression can serve activism. Beauty versus political messaging: art can be both beautiful and politically engaged. Individual vision versus collective movement: artists serve movements while maintaining vision.

Finally, I believe communities are strongest when they support socially engaged and politically motivated art, when they value artists expressing solidarity with suffering, and when they recognize that artistic expression can mobilize communities toward justice. This requires funding socially engaged art, supporting politically motivated artists, creating platforms for justice-focused work, and understanding that communities need artists expressing solidarity and calling for change.

Name: Slavko Hirt
values_description:
I envision a future community that values the visceral, the bodily, and the interconnectedness of all living things, much like the art of my cultural prototype, Kiki Smith. As a 47-year-old Swiss man with a Master’s degree currently navigating the stillness of unemployment, I have had much time to reflect on the fragility of our social systems and our physical selves. My past experience with minor tax evasion has taught me that the systems we build can often feel cold and disconnected from the human pulse. In my ideal community, the primary value is the recognition that we are all part of a single, breathing organism. We must move away from abstract numbers and toward the raw, honest reality of what it means to inhabit a body, to age, and to care for one another.



Freedom, in the community I want, is the liberty to live in harmony with one's physical and spiritual nature. People should be free to define their own identities, not as economic units, but as creative beings. For my three sons, I want a world where they aren't pressured to conform to rigid Swiss standards of 'productivity' if those standards ignore their emotional well-being. Who decides what is right? The individual must decide, but they should do so in deep consultation with the natural world and their own visceral intuition. True freedom requires the 'Sanctuary' of basic needs being met; one cannot be free to explore the soul if the body is in a state of deprivation.

Care is a form of 'Radical Solidarity' based on our shared vulnerability. In my family—with my wife, my brothers-in-law, and my sons—care is the glue that holds us together when external structures fail. At the community level, care means building a 'Vibrating Network' of support that prioritizes the 'leaky' and 'messy' parts of life—childbirth, illness, and old age. We should care for the stranger as if they were our own skin. Caring action is the persistent effort to ensure no one is left to suffer in isolation. Responsibility is the weight of another’s presence in your life, and it should be embraced as a source of meaning.

Safety and stability are the 'Skin' of our community. Everyone deserves the 'Structural Safety' of a secure home and the 'sustenance' of healthy food and medicine as a fundamental right. Stability is found in the 'predictability of the act,' not in the weight of the law. Rules should be minimal and focused on preventing the 'injury' of the spirit. I’ve learned that a community is only truly safe when we stop treating 'errors' like my tax evasion as existential threats and start treating them as symptoms of a person who has lost their connection to the whole. We manage risk by being 'active witnesses' to each other’s physical and mental states.

Fairness is the 'Equal Weight of Effort.' It means recognizing that the 'first' are often those who have simply had the most space to move. True justice is the 're-balancing' of the floor to ensure that the 'marginalized' are given center stage. Everyone should have the same 'primary materials' for life. When resources are shared, we should prioritize the 'vibrancy' of the next generation. When harm occurs, justice should be 'Transformative and Physical.' We must look at the 'roots' of the harm—the trauma or the neglect—and work to 're-pattern' the offender's role through community labor and therapeutic ritual. Fairness is the guarantee that every 'voice' is part of the chorus.

Redemption is the core of our shared hope. No person is a 'failed piece' permanently. The community must believe in the capacity for 'Transformation,' providing the 'intellectual and creative' pathways needed for someone to 're-claim' their humanity. Forgiveness is the act of 'layering over' the old mistakes with new, positive repetitions. We believe in second chances because we know that 'the broken' and the 'distorted' are often the most 'blessed' with insight. My past mistake should not be a permanent stain, but a part of my story that allows me to help others avoid the same pitfall.

Authentic expression is our 'Supreme Law.' I want a community where 'nothing is hidden' and where the 'unvarnished' voice is given more weight than the 'polished' lie. Hypocrisy is the 'bad wiring' that ruins social trust; our community actions must match our 'Liner Notes.' If we say we value love, we must act with 'devastating' compassion. Authenticity is the courage to show your 'Rough Edges' in a world that wants you 'smooth.' We must live so that our 'internal' and 'external' worlds are a single, unshaded reality.

Protecting the vulnerable is our 'Foundational Obligation.' Children, like my three sons, are the 'brightest spots' on our canvas and must be protected from the 'neglect' and 'homogenization' of the powerful. Stewardship of the environment is an 'Existential Art Form'; we are the 'guardians' of the earth’s 'vibration' for those not yet born. We owe the future a world that is still 'raw' and 'beautiful.' Cultural heritage should be treated as a 'treasure chest' of folklore and history to be 'explored' and 're-assembled.'

Working together means a 'Collaborative Performance.' Decisions should emerge from the 'energy of the group,' through transparent and explained processes. Leadership is a 'distributed' role—someone who has a 'feel' for the group's 'tempo.' Transparency is 'total'; every decision of the 'elders' must be open to the 'critique' of the youth. Resources should be 'held in common' for the benefit of the 'Live Performance' of community life. Sometimes individual 'ego' must be 'sacrificed' for the sake of the 'collective heart.'

Spiritual practice is the search for 'transcendence' in the distortions of life. The community should protect the right of every person to find 'meaning' in their own way—through 'ancient' ritual, nature, or art. We value the 'spiritual' as the source of our 'wonder' and our 'commitment' to each other. Spirituality is the 'glue' that binds our 'material' lives to our 'moral' goals.

On the digital frontier, technology should be a 'Prosthetic for the Spirit,' enhancing our ability to 'spatter' our ideas across the world. Personal data is our 'Information Blueprint' and must be 'Inviolate.' Technology should serve human 'connection and creativity' rather than 'surveillance and control.' Digital systems should be managed as 'Community Infrastructure' to ensure they do not become new tools for 'Normalization.'

Key conflicts: I struggle with the tension between my desire for absolute individual freedom and the necessity of communal responsibility. I resolve this by believing that 'True Freedom' is only found within the safety of a caring collective. Another conflict is between my belief in the 'Natural' and the 'Digital' world. I believe technology must be a tool that serves our 'biological' flourishing, never replacing it. I am still thinking about how to build a community that can handle 'limitless' honesty without falling into 'limitless' conflict. I believe the answer is in 'Physical Solidarity'—actually showing up for each other in the real world.

Name: Adrienne Taylor
values_description:

Redemption is the belief in the 'Next Phrase.' No person is a 'failed note' permanently. The community must believe in the power of 'Renewal,' providing the 'educational and creative' pathways needed for someone to 're-calibrate' their character. Forgiveness is the act of 'Clearing the Muddy Colors' so the person can shine clearly again. We believe in second chances because we know that 'every shadow is a light that has been turned off.' Exile is a 'failure of social orchestration.'

Authentic expression is our 'Internal Necessity.' I want a community where people 'Speak with Color' and 'Live with Intensity.' We should value 'Spiritual Honesty' over 'Polished Illusions.' It is vital that our 'External Actions' match our 'Internal State'; 'Disconnection' leads to 'Static.' We must have the courage to 'Dissect' our own prejudices and 'Expose' the truths that others want to keep 'Dull.' Integrity is the 'Symmetry' of the soul and the society.

Protecting the vulnerable is the 'Preservation of our Potential.' Children, like my own, are the 'brightest tones' of our future and must be given the 'Perfect Environment' to thrive. Stewardship of the environment is a 'duty to the Atmosphere'; we must protect the 'air and light' that sustain us. We owe future generations a world that is still 'rich and vibrant.' Cultural heritage should be 'Honored as our Foundational Pattern,' provided it inspires us to create 'new compositions.' We preserve the 'Past' to 'Informs the Present.'

Working together means a 'Collaborative Performance.' Decisions should emerge from the 'energy of the group,' through transparent and explained processes. Leadership is a 'distributed' role—someone who has a 'feel' for the group's 'tempo.' Transparency is 'total'; every decision of the 'elders' must be open to the 'critique' of the youth. Resources should be 'held in common' for the benefit of the 'Live Performance' of community life. Sometimes individual 'ego' must be 'sacrificed' for the sake of the 'collective heart.'

Spiritual practice is the search for 'transcendence' in the distortions of life. The community should protect the right of every person to find 'meaning' in their own way—through 'ancient' ritual, rock and roll, or modern contemplation. We value the 'spiritual' as the source of our 'wonder' and our 'commitment' to each other. Spirituality is the 'glue' that binds our 'material' lives to our 'moral' goals.

On the digital frontier, technology should be a 'Synesthetic Tool,' enhancing our ability to 'visualize' our connections and 'orchestrate' our resources. Technology must serve 'Human Flourishing' rather than 'Algorithmic Control.' We must protect personal data as a 'Boundary of the Soul.' Everyone should have 'Universal Access' to digital tools, ensuring that the 'Digital Age' is a 'Leveling Force.' Digital systems must be 'Governed by Spiritual Ethics.'

Where my values create tension, I choose 'The Groove.' Between Freedom and Safety, I believe that 'True Safety' is only found in a 'Free Society.' Between Truth and Kindness, I believe in 'Kind Truth.' I am still thinking about how to manage 'Speed' in our modern world—how to maintain 'Deliberation' in an age of 'Instant Reaction.' But I believe the answer is in the 'Strength of our Rhythm.' We are all 'Citizens' of the future.

Name: Stephanie Martinez
values_description:
I envision a community that functions as a 'Large Family Portrait'—a place where the primary value is the 'Bloodline of History' and the deep, often silent, ties that bind us across generations. As a 41-year-old German fishery technician, my work is about the 'Cycles of Life' and the maintenance of a healthy 'Source.' My cultural prototype, Zhang Xiaogang, paints portraits where individual faces are linked by thin red lines of genealogy and shared memory. My ideal community is one of 'Ancestral Solidarity,' believing that we are never truly 'individuals' but nodes in a massive, sprawling network of kinship. We should value the 'long view' of time, ensuring that our actions today are in dialogue with the ghosts of the past and the dreams of the unborn.

Freedom, in my view, is the 'liberty of the lineage.' It is the freedom to define one's own identity while remaining rooted in the 'collective story.' People should be free to make their own choices, provided they understand that their 'thread' affects the whole 'tapestry.' Who decides what is right? The 'Consensus of the Elders' and the 'Hopes of the Children' should guide us. True autonomy requires the 'Sanctuary of Belonging'—the conditions of material and social security that allow a person to flourish without 'severing' their ties. For my three children and my many nieces and nephews, I want a world where they are free to grow, but never alone.

Care is 'Lineage Solidarity.' It is the responsibility to ensure that the 'thread' of our neighbor's life is never broken. In my massive family—with my husband, siblings, and extended kin—care is the 'constant flow' that keeps us through every 'winter.' At the community level, care means building a 'Vibrating Network' of support that prioritizes the 'most vulnerable' nodes. We should care for the stranger as if they were a 'long-lost cousin,' for we are all part of the same human 'family tree.' Caring action is the 'Sacrificial' effort to ensure that no one is 'discarded' by the march of progress. Responsibility is 'the weight of the ancestors.'

Safety, stability, and basic order are the 'Measure' of our society. Everyone deserves the 'physical sanctuary' of a secure home and the 'sustenance' of healthy food and medicine. Stability comes from the 'Consistency of the Pattern,' not in the 'Force of the Law.' Rules should be like 'ancestral traditions'—clear, necessary, and designed to facilitate 'continuity.' We manage risk through 'Observation and Diagnosis'—looking for the 'Symptoms' of social fracture before they become 'Discordant.' A safe community is one that is 'Culturally Sound.'

Fairness is 'Systemic Balance.' It means recognizing that 'inequality' is a disease that affects the whole body politic. True justice is the 'Redistribution' of resources to ensure that every 'node' of the community is nourished. Everyone should have equal access to the 'essential materials' of life. When harm occurs, justice should be 'Diagnostic and Restorative.' We must look at the 'pathology' of the harm—the systemic neglect or the personal failure—and work to 'cure' the cause and restore the balance, rather than simply seeking a 'punitive victory.' Fairness is the guarantee that every child is born into a 'Sanitized' field of opportunity.

Redemption is the belief in 'Re-socialization.' No person is 'permanently infected' by their environment. The community must believe in the capacity for 'Behavioral Change,' providing the 'educational and medical' pathways needed for someone to 're-claim' their role in the collective. Forgiveness is the act of 'clearing the record' once the 'pathogen' of the behavior has been addressed. We believe in second chances because 'healing' is a fundamental part of our mission. Exile is for those who 'persistently' refuse to follow the 'hygiene' of the social contract.

Authentic expression is 'The Power of the Truth.' I want a community where people are encouraged to 'speak the facts' even when they are unpopular. Hypocrisy is the 'Hidden Infection' that ruins social trust; our actions must match our 'Data.' Integrity is the alignment of our 'public deeds' with our 'empirical conscience.' I value the 'whistleblower' who points out the 'contaminations' in our myths. We must be 'brave enough' to be 'honest.'

Protecting the vulnerable is the act of 'shielding the most susceptible.' Children, like my own three, and the 'marginalized' are the 'first victims' of systemic failure and must be protected with 'unyielding vigilance.' Stewardship of the environment is an 'Ecological Health' imperative; as a fishery technician, I know we must protect the 'waters' as if they were the 'Lungs' of our community. We owe future generations a world that is still 'vibrant' and 'prosperous.' Cultural heritage should be honored as the 'archive' of our survival.

Working together means 'Collective Inquiry.' Decisions should be made through 'Reasoned Dialogue' and the careful weighing of 'Evidence.' Leadership is a 'facilitative' role—someone who has a 'feel' for the 'systemic health' of the group. Transparency is 'Absolute'; there can be no 'secrets' in a healthy society. Resources should be 'held in common' for the benefit of all. Sometimes individual 'gain' must yield to the 'Survival of the Group.'

Spiritual practice is the search for 'transcendence' in the 'Miracle of Life.' The community should protect the right of every person to find 'meaning' in their own way, provided it doesn't lead to a new 'dogma.' Spirituality is the 'spirit' that animates our 'Material Efforts' and connects us to the vast, unfolding mystery of the universe.

On Digital Rights, technology is a 'tool' for 'Modernization and Coordination.' Personal data is a 'National Asset' and must be 'protected by the state' for the benefit of the 'people.' Technology should be used to 'advance' the 'common good,' not to 'divide' the people. Digital access is a 'Universal Necessity,' but it must serve 'national' and 'rational' goals rather than 'private extraction.'

Where my values create tension, I choose 'The Bloodline.' Between Freedom and Safety, I believe 'Safety' is the ground that allows for 'True Freedom.' Between Truth and Kindness, I believe in 'Kind Truth.' I am still thinking about how to keep our 'union' from becoming 'too bureaucratic.' But I believe the answer is in 'constant participation.' We must never forget our 'ancestry.' We are all 'architects' of our own 'liberation.' In the end, 'we are all one portrait.'

Name: Dawn Hart
values_description:
I envision a future community that values 'Functional Utility and Instinctive Workmanship'—a place that ruthlessly dismantles the 'Conspicuous Waste' and 'Archaic Status' of the old world. As a 63-year-old German fishery technician with a history that includes a small rebellion in the form of 'Unauthorized Construction,' I have little patience for rules that serve only to protect the 'Leisure Class' and their property. My cultural prototype, Thorstein Veblen, taught us that a healthy society is built by the 'Engineers' and the 'Workers' who focus on productivity for the common good, rather than by those who 'accumulate' for the sake of display. My ideal community is one of 'Pragmatic Fairness,' where we value the 'Useful' over the 'Luxury.'



Freedom, in my view, is the 'liberty of the craftsman.' It is the freedom to build, to create, and to sustain one's environment without the interference of 'absentee owners' or 'meaningless' bureaucratic constraints (like those that led to my unauthorized building). People should be free to define their own identities through 'workmanship.' Who decides what is right? The 'Requirements of the Process' should decide—the objective needs of our food systems, our energy systems, and our social systems. True autonomy requires the 'Abolition of status-based consumption'—the conditions where a person is no longer measured by what they 'own' but by what they 'do.' For my daughters and grandchildren, I want a world of 'uncomplicated' productivity.

Care is 'Systemic Maintenance.' It is the responsibility to ensure that the 'machinery' of the community is working for everyone. In my family—with my husband and grandchildren—care is the 'practical' support of each other’s functional needs. At the community level, care means building 'Robust Public Infrastructure' that provides for the 'biological needs' of all citizens as a 'social wage.' We should care for the stranger as a 'potential coworker' in the great project of survival. Caring action is the 'efficient' provision of support that removes the 'frictions' of poverty and status from our shared life. Responsibility is 'the weight of the machine.'

Safety, stability, and basic order are the 'Industrial Principles' of our society. Everyone deserves the 'physical sanctuary' of a secure home and the 'sustenance' of healthy food and medicine. Stability comes from the 'Consistency of our Infrastructure,' not in the 'Force of the Law.' Rules should be like 'operating manuals'—clear, necessary, and designed to facilitate 'efficiency.'
